source.title: It's not a Lottery, it's a Race: Understanding How Gradient Descent Adapts the Network's Capacity to the Task

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how alignment relates to neuron norms and pruning outcomes in trained networks, a different measurement of task-adapted capacity than the claim versions' specified generalization results.
record.gate_note: The reported cluster merging, alignment-to-final-norm relation, and IMP pruning results bear on capacity and lottery-ticket aspects of the claim. The paper does not report results on the listed versions' natural-label test-error comparisons, width sweeps, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch comparisons, dropout effects, or generalization-gap measures. Theoretical equations and cited findings are not separate experimental rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures neuron alignment, norm growth, clustering and pruning susceptibility. These results do not test V1–V8. Its width comparisons measure cluster counts rather than test error, and its merging experiments report accuracy changes without identifying a held-out evaluation set. Better generalization from overparameterization is cited as motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors propose mutual alignment, unlocking and racing as mechanisms for effective-capacity reduction and favorable lottery-ticket initialization in single-hidden-layer ReLU binary classifiers. Racing beyond the simplified early dynamics remains conjectural; the work does not establish held-out generalization effects.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes small-initialization single-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained by gradient descent/SGD on binary CIFAR-10-derived tasks; it studies alignment, norm growth, clustering, and pruning rather than natural-label test error, random-label fitting, or the listed generalization interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scale changes the number of detected clusters; dataset size changes the effective-capacity clustering; the cluster threshold affects cluster counts and merging outcomes; groups evolve at different speeds.

fits_no_version.finding: Neuron clustering varies with dataset size, network width and initialization scale; larger initialization produces more clusters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested binary CIFAR-10-derived tasks, gradient training produces neuron alignment whose measured effective capacity depends on dataset size, width, initialization and clustering threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: At threshold 0.95, merging changes reported accuracy by −3.3 ± 4.6% to +0.5 ± 0.7% across the recorded settings. Both N=4000 settings retain all 300 neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some tested networks permit neuron merging with small reported accuracy changes; the amount of compression depends on the setting and threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Early alignment predicts final norm products and individual-weight pruning susceptibility, particularly at lower target sparsities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within neuron groups, closer early alignment predicts larger final norms; less aligned neurons tend to have more individual weights pruned by IMP.

record.problems: Experiments use a single hidden layer and binary CIFAR-10-derived datasets; the paper does not report test error or a training-test generalization gap. Several alignment and cluster-count results are qualitative descriptions of figures without numeric values. The theory assumes small initial conditions and gradient flow; the paper says its theory does not cover deeper or advanced architectures or dynamics beyond early learning.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Cited prior findings and theoretical propositions without separate measured outcomes are not rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy under the same architectures and recipes.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error and interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures do not identify those effects. This does not negate the reported alignment, clustering or pruning findings. No additional results bearing on a listed version were found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Natural-label versus random-label train/test accuracy; same recipes fitting random labels while generalizing on natural labels.
Width sweep past the zero-training-error threshold and test error as width increases.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier test error and the effects of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons and tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to the recipe.
Dropout effects on held-out error and interaction with training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements compared with training-test generalization gaps and other generalization measures.
Removing and retraining on memorized examples versus random examples, with resulting test-accuracy effects.

rows.subject: single hidden layer ReLU networks, d=300
rows.operation_detail: Counted neuron clusters by cosine-similarity threshold at end of training across dataset sizes.
rows.measure: Number of clusters, treated as effective capacity
rows.note: The text describes effective capacity increasing with dataset complexity until cluster count saturates at d, but specific plotted values are figure-only.
rows.check: Figure 3(a) varies network width d; the subject is incorrectly restricted to d=300. Cluster counts measure effective capacity, not V2's held-out error beyond interpolation.

rows.subject: single hidden layer ReLU networks, d=300
rows.operation_detail: Compared clustering at initialization, before loss drop, and end of training.
rows.value: Text states increasing initialization scale also increases the number of clusters
rows.note: No numerical cluster counts are stated in the text.
rows.check: Initialization-dependent clustering is reported, but it measures none of the versions' effects.

rows.subject: single hidden layer ReLU networks, d=300
rows.operation_detail: Merged neuron clusters based on cosine-similarity threshold and measured change in accuracy.
rows.measure: Relative change in accuracy after merging
rows.note: The result is a relative accuracy change after merging clusters, not a training-test generalization gap.
rows.check: The −3.3 ± 4.6% value is correct. Its baseline is accuracy before merging, although the absolute accuracy and evaluation split are unspecified. This intervention tests none of V1–V8.

conditions.value: t=76 or t=301 depending on experiment

rows.measure: Number of individual parameters pruned per neuron versus early alignment
rows.value: Text states early alignment predicts to a large degree which neurons have many individual parameters pruned at lower target sparsities
rows.locator: Section 5, Comparison to Lottery Tickets; Figure 5
rows.note: The paper distinguishes this from its neuron-level framework: IMP prunes individual weights over the whole network, in rounds of pruning and retraining. The text says prediction works even better after splitting neurons by cluster, which requires cluster knowledge.
rows.check: Predicting individual-weight pruning from neuron alignment tests none of V1–V8. Pruning weights is distinct from V8's removal of memorized training examples.
